The animal's head is tilted upward with its mouth slightly open, displaying long, prominent white whiskers. The fur appears wet, dark brown on the dorsal side and lighter on the neck/chest. A distinct external ear flap is visible behind the eye.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Head is broad with prominent sagittal crest in males.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The subject displays a smooth, rounded forehead typical of a female or juvenile sea lion. There is no visible bony protrusion (sagittal crest) on the top of the skull, which is a secondary sexual characteristic of mature bulls.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: External ear pinnae (visible ear flaps) distinguish from true seals.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: A small, distinct external ear flap is clearly visible just behind and slightly above the eye, confirming this is an otariid (eared seal/sea lion) and not a phocid (true seal).
Long, stiff, light-colored vibrissae are clearly defined against the dark fur and water background, extending from the muzzle.

checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The coat texture appears consistent with wet pinniped fur—short and sleek. The coloration transitions from dark chocolate brown on the head/back to a lighter tan/golden hue on the throat and chest.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Body exhibits streamlined fusiform form of substantial marine mammal proportions.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The visible neck and upper torso show the characteristic thick, tapering shape of a sea lion, lacking the distinct neck constriction seen in some other marine mammals.

checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The neck is smooth and lacks the thick, ruff-like mane of hair characteristic of adult male sea lions. This aligns with the absence of the sagittal crest.
